title: Put each piece of data in the right store
prompt: A teammate drafted Trailhead's storage plan. Select **every** line of the plan that you would approve in code review.
hints: Ask two questions about each piece of data: is it secret, and will you need to query or filter it?
SecureStore is for small secrets; photos are megabytes.
explanation: Preferences are small and harmless, so AsyncStorage (one JSON blob under a versioned key) fits. The hike log is structured data you sort and filter, so it belongs in expo-sqlite with versioned migrations. The refresh token is a secret, so it belongs in expo-secure-store, encrypted by the Keychain or Keystore. Tokens in AsyncStorage sit in plain text; photos in SecureStore exceed the size it's designed for; and a 600-hike log in AsyncStorage means parsing everything for every query.

units-async.text: Store the user's units preference (km or mi) and reminder setting as one JSON value in AsyncStorage under `trailhead.prefs.v1`.
units-async.why: Approve. Small, non-secret preferences are what AsyncStorage is for, and the versioned key makes future changes easy.

log-sqlite.text: Store the hike log in an expo-sqlite table, with schema changes handled by migrations keyed on `PRAGMA user_version`.
log-sqlite.why: Approve. Structured records you query belong in a database, and versioned migrations keep old users' data intact.

token-async.text: Store the refresh token in AsyncStorage so it loads fast at startup.
token-async.why: Reject. AsyncStorage is unencrypted. Startup speed doesn't justify keeping a credential in plain text.

photo-secure.text: Store each trail photo as a base64 string in expo-secure-store so photos are private.
photo-secure.why: Reject. SecureStore is designed for small values; multi-megabyte photos belong on the file system, with only their paths in SQLite.

token-secure.text: Store the refresh token in expo-secure-store and delete it on sign-out.
token-secure.why: Approve. SecureStore encrypts it with the platform keystore, and deleting it on sign-out leaves nothing behind.

log-async.text: Keep all 600 hikes as one JSON array in AsyncStorage and filter it in JavaScript.
log-async.why: Reject. Every read parses the whole log, every write rewrites it, and there's no way to query without loading everything.
